title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This is not a Grothendieck manuscript page. It is page 92 of a typed English text, apparently a translation from Russian: 'addition' renders дополнение (complement), and the index notation 'μ = 1,R' with an overline is the Russian convention. The formulas are filled in by hand. It is misfiled among the 1965 motivic Galois theory notes; the neighbouring pages are Grothendieck's French notes on Weil numbers and CM fields, with which it has no connection.

The mathematics is the standard step in the Kodaira embedding / projective embedding argument. Setup: V is a compact complex manifold, D a divisor with line bundle [D], and ψ_1,…,ψ_R a basis of H^0(V, O_V[nD]) with no common zero. These sections define a holomorphic map f: V → P^{R-1} with image V̄. The page sets up the proof that f*[H] ≅ [nD], where [H] is the hyperplane bundle restricted to V̄.

- U_μ is the complement of the zero set of ψ_μ. Since the ψ_μ have no common zero, the U_μ cover V.
- The zero set of ψ_μ maps to a hyperplane section H_μ of V̄, and the sets Ū_μ = f(U_μ) form an open cover of V̄.
- On this cover, [H] has transition functions ψ_{μ2}/ψ_{μ1} on overlaps.
- The common refinement U_{iμ} = U^(i) ∩ U_μ is formed, where {U^(i)} is the cover on which [D] has transition functions R_ij.
- On the refinement, [nD] has transition functions R^n_{i1 i2}.
- The pulled-back bundle f*[H] (written [H̃]) has transition functions ψ_{μ2}/ψ_{μ1}, computed in local trivializations as ψ^(i1)_{μ2}/ψ^(i1)_{μ1}; the ratio does not depend on the trivialization.

The next (missing) step would show the two cocycles are cohomologous, presumably via the cochain ψ^(i)_μ, using ψ^(i1) = R_{i1i2}^n ψ^(i2). Conclusion: [nD] ≅ f*[H]. This is textbook material, as in Kodaira or Griffiths–Harris.
errors: 'The family {U_μ}, where Ū_μ = fU_μ' should read {Ū_μ}, as the context shows. This is a typo.
f(U_μ) being open in V̄ requires Ū_μ = V̄ minus the hyperplane H_μ, i.e. f(V) ∩ (P minus H_μ) = f(U_μ). This holds, but the page does not state it.
The transition-function conventions (ψ_{μ2}/ψ_{μ1} versus the inverse) are not fixed explicitly. This is harmless, but comparing with R^n_{i1i2} needs a consistent convention.
The argument is incomplete on this page: the cohomology between ₁R and ₂R is not shown here.

ideas.what: The pullback of the hyperplane bundle under the map defined by a basis of sections of [nD] is isomorphic to [nD], checked by comparing Čech transition functions on a common refinement.
ideas.modern_name: f*O(1) ≅ L^n for the morphism defined by a basepoint-free linear system
ideas.where_published: EGA II §4 (morphisms to projective space defined by sections of invertible sheaves), in algebraic form

deep.surprise_reason: This is a misfiled typed page from a translated (likely Russian) complex-geometry text, giving a routine textbook computation. It is not by Grothendieck and is unrelated to the surrounding notes on motivic Galois groups and CM fields.
transcription_corrections: 'U_μ is an addition to the variety of zeros' means 'complement of the zero set' (translation of the Russian дополнение).
'The family {U_μ}, where Ū_μ = fU_μ' should be read as the family {Ū_μ}.
The sections are ψ_μ, rendered in the typescript by a placeholder glyph; the formulas are handwritten insertions.
A handwritten archive page number '106' appears at bottom left; the typescript page number is 92.
